automation_boundary.automated_scope: Login page -> enter registered email -> RECEIVE OTP -> fill the six OTP digit boxes -> land on the authenticated B2B Portal home page.
automation_boundary.external_boundary: OTP delivery itself is external. The automated run needs the code supplied to it; reading the mailbox or the SMS is out of scope.

canonical_steps.action: Navigate to the B2B Portal login page
canonical_steps.expected_result: The login page loads and the email address field is visible

canonical_steps.action: Enter the registered Organization Administrator email address
canonical_steps.expected_result: The email is accepted and the RECEIVE OTP button becomes actionable

canonical_steps.action: Click RECEIVE OTP to request the one-time password
canonical_steps.expected_result: The six OTP digit boxes are displayed and an OTP is issued to the registered address

canonical_steps.action: Enter the six-digit OTP, one digit per box, using boxes 1 to 6 in order
canonical_steps.expected_result: All six boxes are filled and verification is submitted

canonical_steps.action: Dismiss the error dialog with OKAY when the OTP is rejected
canonical_steps.expected_result: The dialog closes and the user is returned to OTP entry without losing the session

canonical_steps.action: Verify the authenticated B2B Portal home page is displayed
canonical_steps.expected_result: The company profile control is visible in the header, confirming an authenticated session

test_data_notes.attribute_spelling: The OTP input name is 'opt-field' -- the application's own spelling, not a typo in this file. Do not 'correct' it to 'otp-field'.
test_data_notes.primary_test_user: An Organization Administrator account; the BRD names ayishabcrm@gmail.com for the QA environment.
